title: The phosphate numbers are about a thousand times too small
description: We convert nitrate from an amount per kilogram of seawater to an amount per cubic metre, but skip that conversion when deriving phosphate from the same nitrate. The label says mol/m³ even though the number is still on the per-kilogram scale.
example: If converted nitrate is 16 units, the model's 16:1 ratio calls for phosphate of 1 unit. The current output is about 0.000966 instead. That can make a nutrient inventory look almost empty.
scientific_evidence: The native nitrate input is in mol kg⁻¹. Published po4 is exactly native no3 / 16, while published no3 includes the model density factor 1,035. In January 0101 piControl, 2,665,319 valid 3-D cells match native no3 / 16 exactly; no3 / (16 × po4) is 1,034.99985–1,035.00008. Surface comparisons at the first and last months of both the first and last files pass the same factor test in all six published experiments (24 comparisons).
impact: Nutrient concentrations, inventories and N:P comparisons are invalid at the advertised units. This is a systematic scaling error, not a range-check artefact.
recommended_action: Correct the mapping to native no3 × 1035 / 16 (or the scientifically approved density convention), preserve masks and regenerate. Check every output against published no3 / 16, including deep water. Do not alter correctly converted no3 or other tracers by the same factor.
development_team_action: MOPPy: review the model-specific phosphate mapping repair. Gadi native units confirm ESM1-6 needs nitrate ×1035/16, while ESM1-5 needs nitrate ×0.001/16 because that archive uses mmol/m3. No model-physics defect was established. Publication team: replace the six listed ESM1-6 releases; ESM1-5 publication impact still needs a separate audit.
extent_statement: Complete file list within the identified release versions; numerical confirmation was sampled, not a scan of every value.
publication_action: No withdrawal, retraction, replacement or ESGF submission performed by this task.
validation: Fresh CMIP7 ESM1-6 and CMIP6 ESM1-5 outputs were checked through all 50 depths against native units and independent conversion. The ESM1-6 output agrees with published nitrate/16 within 4.66e-10 mol/m3. Masks agree; 227 focused tests passed.
